correctness.rationale: The norm bound follows from gamma <= |s|+||x|| <= sqrt(2)||h||. Convexity of gamma squared and the Hilbert parallelogram law prove a quadratic modulus. For a purported unbounded localization sequence, normalized positive directions g_n are weakly null because each coordinate is <=1/(r_n w_j). The exact norm-one support functional F_n has F_n(z_n-p)=N_beta(z_n-p), and F_n(p-y) tends to beta(1-b)/sqrt(1+beta)>0, contradicting localization. Kirk–Ray and the uniformly convex bounded-set fixed-point theorem yield the final universal claim. No finite test is misused as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact new claim couples (i) all ordinary nonexpansive selfmaps on an unbounded positive affine slice, (ii) an explicit 2-uniformly convex ambient norm, and (iii) arbitrarily small Hilbert distortion, with one fixed set independent of the perturbation parameter. The arXiv:2610.14868v1 primary constructs the unbounded set for a max-gauge renorming but neither establishes uniform convexity of that norm nor continuity of the fixed-point phenomenon to Hilbert distortion 1. Explicit positive support-functional limits supply the new property. Saejung (2010) assumes ambient smoothness and studies type (P) maps, hence does not imply this nonsmooth ordinary-nonexpansive classification. Literature and published-research-index searches returned no implication covering the full statement; independent historical priority remains open.
residual_risks: Historical-priority searches do not rule out a general pre-2026 result for nonsmooth strongly convex perturbations of Hilbert metrics.

value.rationale: The construction is the first identified demonstration that arbitrarily small quadratic-modulus uniformly convex perturbations of a Hilbert norm can support an unbounded nonexpansive fixed-point set, even on one and the same positive affine slice. It resolves two natural strong-geometry refinements of the 2026 existence theorem, demonstrates a sharp discontinuity at Hilbert distortion 1, and supplies a reusable support-functional mechanism for small perturbations rather than a routine numerical variant. It does not claim a new general fixed-point theorem or arbitrary nearby-norm robustness.
